code_first.q: Find the smaller of two illustrative file sizes without sorting.
code_first.code:
smallestGB = 9
fileGB = 4
if fileGB < smallestGB then
    smallestGB = fileGB
endif
print(smallestGB)
p: Predict the smaller file size in GB.
Compare a third file of 2 GB; explain why the smallest file size does not determine the best storage device.
code_first.a: Initially 4 GB prints. If fileGB=12, smallestGB remains 9 GB. Adding a further comparison with 2 GB makes smallestGB=2 GB. Choosing storage also depends on total capacity, speed, durability, reliability and cost.

original_exam_questions: Write a condition to test if x is even. [2 marks]
Explain why a loop is preferable to repeating the same five input lines. [2 marks]
Reduces duplicated code and makes repetition count easy to change.
State when a function is preferable to a procedure. [2 marks]
When a calculated value must be returned to the caller.

stretch.task: Extend the program to compare a third file of 2 GB and print the minimum.

mastery.task: Write a function that finds both minimum and maximum of a non-empty array without sorting; explain behaviour for all-equal values.
mastery.hint: Initialise min/max to first item; inspect each other item.
mastery.answer: [4,1,8,1] min1 max8; [7,7] min=max=7. Define handling for empty input.
